title: Query-plan baselining and regression guardrails for control-plane slow paths
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Introduce a system to capture, store, and enforce query plan baselines for the control-plane's top N slow/expensive queries. This ticket implements automated fingerprinting of query text and planner output, a baseline store, CI checks to detect regressions on PRs, runtime guards/alerts when plans deviate beyond configured thresholds, and a safe re-baselining flow for planned optimizer changes.
context: We frequently see flakiness where a harmless schema change or Postgres version bump causes a previously stable plan to degrade (hash->nested loop, lost index usage). Currently detection is manual and often discovered by customer incidents. Several DB schema cleanups and online migrations are scheduled this year; without plan baselines we risk regressions during rollout. Existing work on idempotent online schema updates (ENG-312456) reduces schema-change risk but doesn't catch planner regressions early.
proposed_solution: 1) Build a lightweight query fingerprinting service that normalizes queries (remove literals, collapse whitespace) and stores a hash. 2) For each fingerprint capture a sample EXPLAIN (ANALYZE when safe) and a compact plan signature (node types + important cost/rows metrics). 3) Create a baseline store (Postgres table) with allowed plan signatures and meta (app version, schema snapshot, bounding thresholds). 4) Integrate a CI job that runs on PRs affecting schema or query paths: it runs a small query workload against a test replica and fails if plan signatures deviate beyond thresholds. 5) Add runtime detectors that compare live plans (sampled via pg_stat_statements + pg_catalog queries) to baselines and open alerts in PagerDuty/Console when divergence occurs. 6) Provide a guarded re-baselining workflow (canary run -> review -> commit baseline) and UI endpoints for ops to approve baselines.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fingerprinting service accepts SQL and returns deterministic fingerprint for same logical query.
- Baseline table schema defined and migrations added.
- CI job integrated into main repo; at least one existing slow-query has a baseline and CI correctly fails when we simulate a plan change in test.
- Runtime detector produces alerts for simulated plan drift in staging and creates an entry in Console with query fingerprint, old plan signature, new plan signature, and suggested next steps.
- Re-baselining flow documented (runbook) and demoed to SRE/DBA.
- Unit/integration tests and a migration rollback path exist.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): deploy fingerprinting collector + baseline table to staging, baseline top 10 slow queries from production-sampled traces. Enable CI check for a subset of repos. Phase 2 (controlled): enable runtime detector in staging/qa and route alerts to a low-noise channel; run canary schema change and verify detection. Phase 3 (prod): enable CI checks for all schema PRs, enable runtime alerts to oncall, and schedule quarterly baseline reviews. Each phase has a one-week soak and a go/no-go review.
rollback_plan: Disable CI gate and detector flag via feature flagmanager. Revert baseline table migration if incompatible (use online-migration pattern from ENG-312456). Reissue any schema change rollbacks per existing migration playbooks.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for fingerprinting normalization.
- Integration test that stores and compares plan signatures using a dockerized Postgres with controlled planner settings.
- CI smoke that intentionally forces a planner change by setting enable_* planner flags in the test DB to simulate regressions and verify CI fails.
- Load test: sample 1% of production queries to ensure collector overhead <1% CPU and latency impact <3ms per request.
- End-to-end test: create a PR that modifies an index or query and observe CI rejection until baseline updated via documented flow.
telemetry_and_metrics:
- Number of baselined fingerprints.
- % of sampled queries with matching baseline.
- CI gate failure rate and false-positive rate.
- Mean time to detect plan drift.
- Collector overhead metrics (p99 latency, CPU).
- Alert counts routed to PagerDuty.
- Dashboard in Console: active divergences, recent re-baselines.
open_questions:
- What threshold for 'significant deviation' should we use (cost multiplier, row estimate delta, node-type change)? Recommend start with node-type changes + cost>3x.
- How to handle EXPLAIN ANALYZE collection for queries with side-effects? Use explain without analyze and compare planner-only signatures there.
- Storage: should baseline store be in control-plane DB or a separate metadata DB? Initial plan is control-plane with compact schema; consider moving to dedicated metadata DB later.
- Who signs off re-baselines for cross-tenant-impacting queries (SRE + Product)?
